title: Bitonic Sorter
subtitle: Ken Batcher's fixed wiring of comparators, and what a circuit of sums and relu pays to run it.

chapters.title: Two Wires and a Fold
chapters.blurb: A comparator, a mountain-shaped sequence, and the half-cleaner that splits a mountain into two independent halves.

chapters.title: Building the Mountains
chapters.blurb: Eight shuffled numbers become mountains of two, then four, then eight, and finally one sorted line in six stages.

chapters.title: The Staircase
chapters.blurb: How many stages and comparators a bitonic sorter needs as the list doubles, why a lockstep processor likes it, and two traps for implementers.

chapters.title: What Handwired Pays
chapters.blurb: A comparator as three layers of sums and relu, the measured price of a bitonic network, and why ranks by counting win at interface sizes.
